en: to be mobilized; to be called up

examples.en: All the staff were pulled in to prepare for the festival.

examples.ko: 눈이 많이 와서 제설 장비가 동원돼요.
examples.en: Because of heavy snow, snow-clearing equipment is brought out.
I was suddenly roped into cleaning on the weekend.

examples.ko: 큰 행사에는 많은 사람이 동원되는 편이에요.
examples.en: Big events tend to bring in lots of people.

examples.ko: 사고 현장에 소방차 열 대가 동원됐어요.
examples.en: Ten fire trucks were sent to the accident scene.

examples.ko: 억지로 동원된 사람들은 표정이 좋지 않았어요.
examples.en: The people who were forced to come didn't look happy.

explain: '동원되다'는 본인이 원해서가 아니라 위에서 시켜서 불려 나간다는 느낌이 있어요. 자기가 스스로 나서면 '참여하다'나 '나서다'를 써요.

phrases.en: The company mobilized its staff to clean.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이나 물건을 불러 모으는 쪽에서 쓰는 말이에요. '동원되다'와 짝이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used by the side that gathers people or things. It pairs with 동원되다.

phrases.en: I was called out to an event on the weekend, so I couldn't rest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이유를 설명할 때 연결해서 써요. 시켜서 억지로 나갔다는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Links to a reason. It carries the feeling of being made to go.

phrases.en: I was suddenly called out to the event.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때는 이 표현이 더 쉽고 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: In speech this is easier and more natural.

explain_en: '동원되다' carries the feeling of being called out by someone above, not volunteering. If you step up on your own, use '참여하다' or '나서다'.

examples.en: Construction gets into full swing from next month.
As competition got going in earnest, prices went down.
We need to prepare before the rainy season fully sets in.
Discussion of the new business has finally gotten into full swing.

examples.ko: 선거 운동이 곧 본격화될 거라고 해요.
examples.en: They say the election campaign will soon get into full swing.
I'll contact you again when the negotiations get serious.

explain: 일이나 흐름이 시작 단계를 지나 제대로 진행될 때 써요. 주어는 공사, 경쟁, 논의처럼 일이나 현상이에요. 사람이 의도를 갖고 하면 '본격화하다'를 써요.

phrases.en: The new road construction is getting into full swing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 진행 중인 변화를 말할 때 '-고 있다'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '-고 있다' to describe a change in progress.

phrases.en: Discussion about next year's budget has picked up in earnest.
phrases.nuance_ko: '논의, 경쟁, 조사'처럼 일이나 현상과 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Goes well with things or events such as discussions, competition, or investigations.

phrases.en: The rainy season starts in earnest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 뜻을 '본격적으로'로 풀어 말한 거예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A way to express the same idea with '본격적으로'.

explain_en: Use it when something moves past the starting stage and really gets going. The subject is an event or phenomenon, such as construction, competition or discussion. When a person does it on purpose, use '본격화하다'.

t90.ax: Construction gets into full swing from next month.

en: to be executed; to be enforced; to be implemented

examples.en: A new system will be implemented from next week.
The exam was carried out nationwide at the same time.
This test is carried out every year.
The results of the survey that was conducted were announced.
It's the period when free checkups are offered.
The inspection couldn't be carried out because of the rain.

explain: '하다'의 공식적인 말로, 조사·시험·제도·검사처럼 계획된 일이 실제로 시작될 때 써요. '시행되다'는 법과 제도가 효력을 가질 때, '실시되다'는 조사·시험 같은 행동이 이뤄질 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '하다'를 써요.

phrases.en: The school holds an exam next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이나 기관이 직접 하는 능동형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The active form, where a person or institution carries it out.

phrases.en: The new law takes effect from next year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 법이나 제도가 효력을 가질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a law or system takes effect.

phrases.example: 요즘 전국에서 건강 검사가 실시되고 있어요.
phrases.en: Health checkups are being carried out nationwide these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 진행 중인 일에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for something currently in progress.

explain_en: A formal version of '하다' for planned things like surveys, exams, systems and inspections actually being carried out. '시행되다' is for laws and rules taking effect; '실시되다' for actions like surveys and tests. In daily talk, people just say '하다'.

dis.h: plan, exam, or system put into effect
gh: a task or duty gets carried out

p.n: 수행되다 stresses the work being carried out.

t90.ax: This test is carried out every year.

en: to join the military; to enlist

examples.en: My younger brother enlists next week.
I enlisted after finishing my second year of university.
I cut my hair short before enlisting.

examples.ko: 친구가 입영한 뒤로 편지를 자주 써요.
examples.en: I write letters often since my friend enlisted.
My parents saw me off on the day I enlisted.
I couldn't enlist because my health was poor.

explain: 병무청 같은 공식 안내와 뉴스에서 자주 쓰고, 대화에서는 '군대 가다'가 더 흔해요. 같은 상황의 '입대하다'도 써요. 반대로 군 생활을 마치는 것은 '제대하다'예요.

phrases.en: My older brother enlisted last year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 입영하다와 거의 같은 뜻이고 대화와 뉴스에서 모두 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same meaning as 입영하다 and used in both conversation and news.

phrases.en: My older brother is going into the army next year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 입영하다보다 편한 말이라서 친구와 이야기할 때 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: More casual than 입영하다 and natural when talking with friends.

phrases.en: I met my friends before I enlisted.
phrases.nuance_ko: 입영하기 전의 시간을 말할 때 쓰는 연결 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connecting form used to talk about the time before enlisting.

explain_en: It is common in official notices such as from the Military Manpower Administration and in the news, while '군대 가다' is more common in conversation. '입대하다' is also used for the same situation. Finishing service is '제대하다'.

t90.ax: My younger brother enlists next week.

examples.ko: 이사하고 나서 주민센터에서 전입 신고를 했어요.
examples.en: After moving, I reported my change of address at the community center.

examples.ko: 구청에서 전입 절차를 안내해 줘서 쉽게 끝냈어요.
examples.en: The district office explained the move-in procedure, so I finished it easily.

examples.ko: 전입 학생이 많아서 새 학기에 반을 늘렸어요.
examples.en: There were many transfer students, so they added a class for the new term.

examples.ko: 이번 달에 전입이 많아서 동네가 활기가 넘쳐요.
examples.en: Many people moved in this month, so the neighborhood is full of life.

examples.ko: 전입 신고를 해야 아이가 근처 학교에 배정돼요.
examples.en: You have to report your move-in so your child is assigned to a nearby school.

examples.ko: 전입보다 전출이 많은 지역은 인구가 줄어요.
examples.en: In areas where more people move out than in, the population shrinks.

explain: 반의어는 '전출'이에요. 이사한 뒤 새 주소지에 주민등록을 옮기는 '전입 신고'라는 말로 가장 자주 들어요.

phrases.example: 이사한 날 바로 전입 신고를 했어요.
phrases.en: I filed my move-in report on the day I moved.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새 주소로 옮겼다고 알리는 일로, 가장 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Reporting a move to a new address, the most common usage.

phrases.en: Please tell me the date you moved in.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새 주소로 옮겨 등록한 날을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The date you registered at the new address.

phrases.example: 이 도시는 전입 인구가 계속 늘고 있어요.
phrases.en: The number of people moving into this city keeps growing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새로 옮겨 온 사람들의 수를 말할 때 뉴스에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in news for the number of newcomers moving in.

explain_en: The opposite is '전출' (moving out). You will hear it most often in '전입 신고', the report you make to register your new address after moving.

examples.ko: 지하철 운행이 곧 정상화된다는 안내가 나왔어요.
examples.en: An announcement said subway service would soon return to normal.

examples.ko: 공장 가동이 정상화되어 직원들이 모두 안심했어요.
examples.en: The factory resumed normal operation, and all the employees felt relieved.
Once the rain stops, train service returns to normal.

examples.ko: 인터넷이 아직 정상화되지 않아서 일을 못 해요.
examples.en: The internet hasn't returned to normal yet, so I can't work.

examples.ko: 두 나라의 관계가 하루빨리 정상화되면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I hope relations between the two countries return to normal soon.
I got a text saying the service was back to normal.

explain: 서비스, 운행, 관계, 경제처럼 문제가 있다가 원래대로 돌아올 때 뉴스에서 많이 써요. 사람이 일부러 되돌릴 때는 '정상화하다'를 쓰고, 일상 대화에서는 '복구되다'도 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: Service is scheduled to return to normal tomorrow morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안내 방송이나 뉴스에서 앞으로의 일을 알릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in announcements and news to tell what will happen next.
phrases.en_equiv: is expected to return to normal

phrases.en: The internet was restored within an hour.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 고장 난 것이 다시 되는 일에 이 말을 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily talk this is used more for things that broke and work again.

phrases.en: My health has returned to normal now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쉽게 풀어서 말하는 표현이라 대화에서 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier, spelled-out expression that sounds natural in conversation.

explain_en: News often uses it when services, operations, relations or the economy return to normal after a problem. When someone deliberately restores things, use '정상화하다', and in daily talk '복구되다' is also common.

examples.en: There is a big flagpole on the school playground.
Every morning they raise the Korean flag on the flagpole.

examples.ko: 바람이 세서 게양대의 깃발이 심하게 흔들려요.
examples.en: The wind is strong, so the flag on the flagpole is flapping hard.
Let's meet in front of the flagpole at the park entrance.

examples.ko: 새로 만든 게양대는 높이가 십 미터쯤 돼요.
examples.en: The newly built flagpole is about ten meters tall.

examples.ko: 국경일에는 관공서 게양대마다 국기가 걸려 있어요.
examples.en: On national holidays, a flag hangs on every flagpole at government offices.

explain: 국기나 깃발을 다는 기둥이에요. '깃대'라고도 해요. '게양'이 국기를 높이 단다는 말이라서 '국기 게양대'처럼 국기와 자주 함께 나와요.

phrases.en: I took a picture in front of the flagpole.
phrases.nuance_ko: 국기와 함께 가장 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the phrase that appears most often with the national flag.

phrases.en: A flag flutters at the top of the pole.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷한 우리말이에요. 국기가 아닌 깃발에도 두루 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a similar native Korean word that also works for flags other than the national flag.

phrases.en: Please hang the flag on the flagpole.
phrases.nuance_ko: 게양대에 깃발을 거는 동작을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to talk about putting a flag up on the pole.

explain_en: It is the pole on which a national flag or other flag is hung. People also say '깃대'. Because '게양' is about raising a flag high, you often see it as '국기 게양대'.

en: heating and cooling unit (air conditioner and heater)

examples.ko: 우리 사무실에는 냉온풍기가 한 대 있어요.
examples.en: There is one heating and cooling unit in our office.
In winter we heat the room with the heating and cooling unit.

examples.ko: 냉온풍기 필터를 한 달에 한 번 청소해요.
examples.en: I clean the unit's filter once a month.

examples.ko: 여름에 냉온풍기를 켜면 방이 금방 시원해져요.
examples.en: In summer, when I turn the unit on, the room cools down quickly.
The unit broke down, so I called the service center.

examples.ko: 새 냉온풍기는 소리가 별로 안 나요.
examples.en: The new unit doesn't make much noise.

explain: 찬바람과 따뜻한 바람이 둘 다 나오는 기계예요. 그냥 '에어컨'이라고 부르는 사람도 많지만, 겨울에 난방까지 되는 제품을 가리킬 때 이 말을 써요.

phrases.en: It's cold, so please turn on the heater/AC unit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기계를 작동시킬 때 쓰는 가장 기본적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic collocation for turning the machine on.
phrases.en_equiv: to turn on the heating and cooling unit

phrases.en: We installed a heating and cooling unit in the office.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기계를 새로 달 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when putting the machine in place.
phrases.en_equiv: to install a heating and cooling unit

phrases.en: I cleaned the heating and cooling unit's filter before summer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기계 관리 이야기에서 자주 나오는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often comes up when talking about maintaining the machine.

explain_en: It is a machine that blows both cool and warm air. Many people simply say '에어컨', but this word is used for a unit that also heats in winter.

examples.en: The mother is nursing the baby.

examples.ko: 밤마다 수유 때문에 잠을 잘 못 자요.
examples.en: I cannot sleep well because of night feedings.

examples.ko: 수유 중에는 약을 먹기 전에 의사와 의논해요.
examples.en: While breastfeeding, talk to a doctor before taking medicine.
There are more shopping malls with nursing rooms.
If breastfeeding is hard, it is fine to give formula.

examples.ko: 아기가 밤에 두 번 수유를 해요.
examples.en: The baby is fed twice at night.

explain: '젖 먹이다'는 입말이고 '수유'는 병원·육아 글에서 쓰는 말이에요. '수유하다', '수유 중', '수유실'처럼 붙여 써요. 젖병으로 먹일 때도 쓸 수 있지만 '모유 수유'가 가장 흔해요.

phrases.en: Breastfeeding is good for babies.
phrases.nuance_ko: '수유' 중에서 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing with 수유.

phrases.en: The department store has a nursing room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아기에게 젖을 먹이도록 만든 공간이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A space made for feeding babies.

phrases.example: 수유 중에는 커피를 줄이는 게 좋아요.
phrases.en: While nursing, it is better to cut down on coffee.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-중'을 붙여 지금 젖을 먹이는 시기라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -중 means the period of currently nursing.

explain_en: 젖 먹이다 is the spoken form, and 수유 is the word used in hospitals and parenting writing. It is attached to other words, as in 수유하다, 수유 중 and 수유실. It can also be used for bottle feeding, but 모유 수유 is the most common.

en: to extend a building; to add on

examples.en: Our house was small, so we added a room.
The school will extend the library.
You need a permit to extend a building.
We added on to this floor and enlarged the shop.
We put a window in the part we added.
After the hospital was extended, patients increased.

explain: 공사 용어라서 말할 때는 '넓히다', '더 짓다'를 쓰는 때도 많아요. 새로 짓는 건 '신축하다', 고치는 건 '수리하다'로 구분해서 말해요.

phrases.en: We're having a child, so I want to extend our house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바람을 말할 때 '-고 싶다'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '-go sipda' to express a wish.

phrases.en: We added on, so there is one more room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이유나 결과를 이어서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to connect a reason or result.

phrases.en: I made the room bigger and put in a desk.
phrases.nuance_ko: '증축하다'보다 쉬운 일상 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier everyday expression than 'jeungchukhada'.

explain_en: It is a construction term, so in speech people often say 넓히다 or '더 짓다' instead. Building new is 신축하다, and repairing is 수리하다.

examples.ko: 농장은 수확한 사과를 내일 시장에 출하해요.
examples.en: The farm ships the harvested apples to the market tomorrow.

examples.ko: 회사는 새 모델을 다음 달부터 출하할 예정이에요.
examples.en: The company plans to start shipping the new model next month.

examples.ko: 공장에서 막 출하한 제품이라 포장이 깨끗해요.
examples.en: It's a product just shipped from the factory, so the packaging is clean.

examples.ko: 농민들이 가격이 오를 때까지 출하하지 않고 기다렸어요.
examples.en: The farmers waited without shipping their crops until prices went up.

examples.ko: 이 공장은 하루에 차를 천 대씩 출하했어요.
examples.en: This factory shipped a thousand cars a day.

examples.ko: 출하하기 전에 불량품이 없는지 꼭 확인해요.
examples.en: Before shipping, we always check that there are no defective items.

explain: 농산물이나 공장 제품을 시장이나 판매처로 내보낼 때 써요. 만들거나 기르는 쪽이 주어예요. 가게가 손님에게 파는 것은 '팔다'나 '판매하다'이고, '배송하다'는 주문한 사람에게 가져다주는 것이라 달라요.

phrases.en: These tangerines were shipped out from Jeju yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건이 내보내지는 쪽에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when viewing it from the side of the goods being sent out.

phrases.example: 딸기는 겨울에서 봄 사이가 출하 시기예요.
phrases.en: The shipping season for strawberries is between winter and spring.
phrases.nuance_ko: 농산물을 시장에 내보내는 때를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The time when produce is sent to market.

phrases.en: Farmers are busy as shipping time approaches.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곧 내보낼 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when shipping is coming soon.

explain_en: It is used when farm produce or factory goods are sent out to a market or seller, and the producer is the subject. A shop selling to a customer is '팔다' or '판매하다', and '배송하다' means bringing an order to the buyer, which is different.

t90.ax: This factory shipped a thousand cars a day.

examples.en: This phone comes equipped with a new camera.

examples.ko: 화물을 배에 탑재하는 데 하루가 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took a day to load the cargo onto the ship.

examples.ko: 새 차에 인공지능 기능을 탑재할 거예요.
examples.en: They will install an AI feature in the new car.

examples.ko: 새로 나온 노트북은 빠른 칩을 탑재해서 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: The new laptop is popular because it has a fast chip built in.

examples.ko: 비행기에 짐을 탑재하기 전에 무게를 재요.
examples.en: They weigh the luggage before loading it onto the plane.

examples.ko: 탑재한 프로그램이 너무 많아서 컴퓨터가 느려요.
examples.en: The computer is slow because it has too many programs installed.

explain: 짐을 배나 비행기에 실을 때도 쓰지만, 요즘은 '기능을 탑재하다'처럼 제품 소개에서 더 자주 들려요. 말할 때는 '넣다', '들어 있다'가 더 흔해요. 사람을 태울 때는 '탑재하다'가 아니라 '태우다'를 써요.

phrases.en: This robot is equipped with artificial intelligence.
phrases.nuance_ko: 제품에 기술을 넣었다고 소개할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing often used in product descriptions for built-in technology.

phrases.example: 이 기능은 모든 휴대폰에 탑재되어 있어요.
phrases.en: This feature is built into every phone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 들어 있는 상태를 말할 때 쓰는 피동 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A passive expression for something already included.

phrases.en: A phone with a new camera built in has come out.
phrases.nuance_ko: '탑재하다'를 뒤의 말을 꾸미는 모양으로 바꾼 것으로, 광고에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifying form, which often appears in advertisements.

explain_en: It is used for loading cargo onto a ship or plane, but nowadays you hear it more in product descriptions like '기능을 탑재하다' (to be equipped with a feature). In casual speech, '넣다' or '들어 있다' is more common. For people, use '태우다' (to give a ride), not '탑재하다'.

dis.h: mount equipment onto a plane, ship, or computer
gh: load cargo onto a ship for shipping

p.n: The other word just means putting on, without the sense of mounting equipment.

t90.ax: This phone comes equipped with a new camera.

en: to decide; to determine; to finalize

examples.ko: 회의 날짜를 이번 주 금요일로 확정해요.
examples.en: We are fixing the meeting date for this Friday.
The team leader finalized the plan.
Let me know when you finalize the schedule.
Nothing has been decided yet.
We will finalize the result next week.
I'll post the ad after we fix the price.

explain: 아직 바뀔 수 있던 것을 마지막으로 정할 때 써요. '정하다'보다 격식 있어서 일정, 가격, 결과 이야기에 어울려요. 정해진 상태는 '확정되다'예요.

phrases.en: I'll let you know once the time is confirmed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정해진 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the state of having been decided.

phrases.en: Please finalize the schedule today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마지막으로 정해 달라고 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A request to make a final decision.

phrases.en: I haven't been able to finalize the price yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 마지막으로 정하지 못했다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the final decision hasn't been made yet.

explain_en: Use it when you settle something that could still change. It is more formal than '정하다' and fits schedules, prices, and results. The settled state is '확정되다'.

dis.h: settle for good; make final and confirmed
gh: everyday word for choosing or fixing something
decide a case as a judge

p.n: 결정 doesn't say the date is final and can't change.
